Allergies: morphine / Dilaudid
Pancreatitis
None

Pt is a ___ y/o F with PMHx significant for HTN, HLD, IBS, who 
was transferred to ___ for further management of pancreatitis.

Pt reports abdominal pain, nausea, vomitting, and diarrhea that 
began yesterday evening.
Emesis was mildly bilious, non-bloody.
Diarrhea was non-bloody.

Describes abdominal pain as diffusely 
located across the abdomen.

She initially presented to OSH, 
where she was tachycardic to 110s initially.

Labs there were 
significant for WBC 23,000, lipase 5900.

Abdominal CT scan was 
performed which showed gallbladder wall edema.

She received IVF, 
analgesics, and zosyn IV prior to transfer.
On arrival to the ___ ED, VS were 97.2 90 141/102 15 96% 2L.
ALT 205 AST 270 Alk Phos 117 Lipase 3230.
Lactate was
3.3, downtrended to 2.7 with IVFs.

RUQ U/S was performed which 
showed fally liver, gall bladder wall edema without stones.

ERCP 
was consulted in the ED and did not want to take the patient for 
urgent ERCP.

Surgery was consulted who recommended admission to 
medicine for MRCP.
VS prior to transfer 98.4, 102, 154/68, 96%

On arrival to the MICU, the patient endorsed diffuse abdominal 
pain that was improved after dilaudid.

Nausea had resolved after 
zofran.
She did not report any other complaints at this time.

II.
Imaging
A. CXR (___)
UNDERLYING MEDICAL CONDITION:

___ year old woman with pancreatitis now with nausea and 
abdominal pain and
   bloating
REASON FOR THIS EXAMINATION:
evaluate for pancreatitis, obstruction, perforation
Final Report

INDICATION:  ___ woman with pancreatitis, now with 
nausea and
abdominal pain and bloating.

Evaluate for pancreatitis, 
obstruction or
perforation.
COMPARISON:  None.
TECHNIQUE:  Portable erect and supine radiographs were provided.

There is a
nonspecific gas pattern within colon and small bowel, but no 
evidence of
obstruction or free air.

Retrocardiac opacity may represent 
consolidation or
left lower lobe atelectasis.

There is levoscoliosis of the 
spine and
degenerative changes.
IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of obstruction or free air.

2. Retrocardiac opacity may represent consolidation or left 
lower lobe
atelectasis.
B. MRCP (___)
Final Report

HISTORY:  ___ woman with likely gallstone pancreatitis, 
please perform
MRCP.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted images were acquired 
on a 1.5

Tesla magnet including dynamic sequential imaging obtained prior 
to, during,
and after the uneventful intravenous administration of 0.1 
mmol/kg (8 mL) of
Gadavist.
FINDINGS:

There is a large hiatus hernia with approximately 50% of the 
stomach within
the thorax.

The liver is not nodular in contour but 
demonstrates diffusely
increased signal intensity on T2-weighted images and loss of 
signal on
out-of-phase compared to in-phase T1-weighted images, consistent 
with hepatic
steatosis.
No focal liver lesions are seen.

No biliary duct 
dilatation.

The
common bile duct measures 5 mm.

The pancreas is diffusely mildly enlarged and demonstrates 
abnormally
increased signal intensity on T2-weighted images and decreased 
signal
intensity on T1-weighted images, consistent with pancreatitis.

The pancreas
enhances homogenously on delayed imaging.

No focal pancreatic 
lesions are
seen.

There is marked peripancreatic fat stranding and a small 
amount of free
fluid in the abdomen.

There is gallbladder wall edema and 
pericholecystic
fluid that is confluent with the remainder of the peripancreatic 
fluid and
likely secondary to the coexisting pancreatitis.

No 
choledocholithiasis.

No
cholelithiasis.

There is a duodenal diverticulum just posterior 
to the
ampulla.

There are numerous small T2 hyperintense lesions throughout the 
spleen.

Following contrast administration, these are hyperenhancing on 
the arterial
phase and demonstrate progressive enhancement on more delayed 
phases,
consistent with hemangiomas; given the multiplicity of lesions, 
this is
consistent with splenic hemangiomatosis.

Both adrenal glands 
and both kidneys
are unremarkable in appearance.

No upper abdominal 
lymphadenopathy.

The
visualized bone marrow is unremarkable.

There is a moderate 
scoliosis in the
lumbar spine.
IMPRESSION:

1.  Pancreatitis without evidence of necrosis or other 
complications.
No cholelithiasis or choledocholithiasis.
2.  Splenic hemangiomatosis.
3.  Large hiatus hernia.

4.  Gallbladder wall edema is noted along with pericholecystic 
fluid,
confluent with peripancreatic inflammatory change and likely 
secondary to
pancreatitis.
5.  Hepatic steatosis.
6.  Duodenal diverticulum.
C. RUQ US (___)

INDICATION:  ___ woman with elevated transaminitis and 
elevated
lipase.
COMPARISON:  CT from an outside hospital ___

FINDINGS:  The liver demonstrates diffuse increase in 
echogenicity, consistent
with fatty infiltration.
No focal liver lesions identified.

There is no
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.

The common bile 
duct is normal
measuring 5 mm.

There is diffuse gallbladder wall edema, which 
is likely due
to known pancreatitis.
No gallstones are identified.
No hydronephrosis or stones are seen.

The head 
of the pancreas
is normal, but the remainder of the pancreas is obscured by 
overlying bowel
gas.
The main portal vein has normal hepatopetal flow.
IMPRESSION:
1. Echogenic liver, consistent with fatty infiltration.

However, other forms
of liver disease including advanced liver disease or cirrhosis 
are not
excluded.
2. Mild gallbladder wall edema likely due to known pancreatitis.

No
gallstones or biliary dilatation.

___ history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, IBS that was 
transferred to ___ for further management of pancreatitis 
likely drug-induced although unknown discrete precipitant with 
hospital course complicated by multi-articular gout especially 
lower extremities.

Patient required MICU admission given BiSAP 
score of ___onsisting of conservative 
and supportive measures.

At hospital discharge, patient was able 
to digest soft diet and had improving joint pain from gout
# Drug-induced pancreatitis

The patient presented with classic symptoms of pancreatitis 
likely secondary to a medication although may also be 
idiopathic.

Lipase was elevated to 3230 with a significant 
transaminitis (ALT 205, AST 270, Tbili 0.6).

Laboratory revealed 
triglycerides 186 and normal calcium.

MRCP and RUQ did not 
reveal gallstone or biliary abnormalities although there was 
gallbladder wall edema likely secondary to pancreatitis.

GI was 
consulted and was concerned that this may be medication-induced 
pancreatitis.
She was fluid resuscitated with 6 L NS along with
IV dilaudid for pain control.

She was briefly placed on zosyn 
given toxic appearance.

Her symptoms improved significant by 
hospital day 2 with resolution of aforementioned laboratory 
abnormalities.

She was subsequently transferred to the medical floor where her 
diet was advanced to a soft diet.

She was very anxious about 
eating but tolerated a soft diet well.

She was told to advance 
her diet as tolerated.

In addition, her NSAIDs and benazapril were held although 
uncertain if pancreatitis is idiopathic or really drug-induced.
These drugs should be re-initiated cautiously.
# Hypertension

The patient was hypertensive during hospitalization given 
benzapril was held.

She was started on norvasc 10 mg PO qD with 
good effect in addition to acebutolol.
# Gout

Patient complained of great bilateral toe pain that was 
concerning for gout attack.
She was on allopurinol ___ mg PO qD.

Her gout worsened and involved the bilateral MTPs, bilateral 
ankles, right knee, and bilateral elbows.

Indomethicin was 
started without good effect.

Rheumatology was consulted and 
advanced IV steroids followed by a steroid taper.
She will ___ with rheumatology at
___ for further management.

Her allopurinol was held given 
that it might have triggered her attack.

# Fever: Patient had fever on ___ attributed to crystalline 
arthritis and resolving pancreatitis.

CXR did reveal a 
retrocardiac opacity that could be atelectasis vs. evolving 
infiltrate; however, clinically, she did not have any localizing 
symptoms to suggest a specific infection.

Blood and urine 
cultures were negative.

She subsequently was afebrile although 
assessment is limited in setting of steroid therapy.
CHRONIC ISSUES
# Hyperlipidemia: She was continued on her home statin
# Pending studies

- Blood cultures dated ___ x 2 are pending and no growth to 
date
